chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said:

I asked him about a man who left a slave among several people, and one of them testified that the deceased had emancipated him. He said: If the witness is trustworthy, he is not liable to compensate, and his testimony is accepted regarding his own share; and the slave is made to work concerning what belonged to the heirs.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one co-owner testifies that a deceased person freed a jointly owned slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about partial emancipation when a jointly held slave is claimed to have been freed by the deceased. If the testifying co-owner is trustworthy, his testimony is accepted regarding his own share without financial liability, while the slave must earn the value of the remaining shares for the heirs.
